system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

content.text:
**Finding: compliant — no redline proposed.**

The agreement contains no audit, inspection, verification or records-examination right running against Bluefly. Targeted searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "records", "monitor" and "premises" turned up nothing usable, and the sections that could plausibly host such a right (§ 4 charges/payment, § 11.5 Capacity Planning, § 12.1 License, §§ 13–14 general terms) contain none.

The planner's likely hook, § 11.3 Suspected Violations, is a breach-remedy provision only: IBM may investigate suspected breaches of the § 11.2(b) content warranties and then restrict access to the Services, require removal of Content, terminate, or pursue other remedies — with an undertaking to attempt notice before restricting access or removing Content. It gives IBM no access to our systems, personnel, books or records, and imposes no audit cost or cooperation burden on us.

That leaves us better off than the AUDIT preferred position (annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, vendor cost, no system access), so inserting an audit framework would only manufacture a right IBM does not have. I noted in the rationale, as a non-deviation observation, that § 11.3's investigation right is uncapped in frequency and its notice commitment is best-efforts only — acceptable given it carries no entry into our environment.

system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed contract finding.
Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?
The claimed status matters: for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is expected, and you should pass when the cited text supports compliance. Fail a deviation finding whose cited clause already meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms (the playbook's classification semantics) — a redline that merely upgrades an acceptable fallback to preferred wording is over-flagging. Compliant findings are retained as internal evaluation evidence, not raised as negotiation issues. For deviation or missing findings, require an actionable valid proposal.
Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
The Agreement grants IBM no audit, inspection, verification or usage-examination right against Bluefly: searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "records", "monitor" and "premises" return nothing relevant, and no such right appears in §§ 4 (Charges/Payment), 11 (IBM obligations/Suspected Violations), 12 (License) or 13-14. The closest hook, § 11.3, is only a right for IBM to investigate suspected breaches of the Customer content/acceptable-use warranties and to restrict access, remove Content or terminate, coupled with an attempt-to-notify commitment (p0137); it confers no access to Bluefly's systems, personnel, books or records and imposes no audit cost or cooperation burden on us. Because there is no audit right binding the Customer, the position is better than the preferred position (annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Vendor cost, no system access), so nothing needs to be inserted or limited — adding an audit framework would only create a right IBM does not currently have. Residual note (not a deviation): § 11.3's investigation right is uncapped in frequency and the notice undertaking is best-efforts only, but as it is a breach-remedy provision without any access to our environment we would leave it as drafted.

p0132: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b). If IBM reasonably determines that a breach of any such warranty has occurred, then IBM may, in its sole and reasonable discretion:
p0137: Except in an emergency or as may otherwise be required by law, before undertaking the activities in Subsection 11.3(a) or 11.3(b), IBM will attempt to notify Customer by any reasonably practical means under the circumstances, such as, without limitation, by telephone or e-mail.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:

input.rationale: The Agreement grants IBM no audit, inspection, verification or usage-examination right against Bluefly: searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "records", "monitor" and "premises" return nothing relevant, and no such right appears in §§ 4 (Charges/Payment), 11 (IBM obligations/Suspected Violations), 12 (License) or 13-14. The closest hook, § 11.3, is only a right for IBM to investigate suspected breaches of the Customer content/acceptable-use warranties and to restrict access, remove Content or terminate, coupled with an attempt-to-notify commitment (p0137); it confers no access to Bluefly's systems, personnel, books or records and imposes no audit cost or cooperation burden on us. Because there is no audit right binding the Customer, the position is better than the preferred position (annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Vendor cost, no system access), so nothing needs to be inserted or limited — adding an audit framework would only create a right IBM does not currently have. Residual note (not a deviation): § 11.3's investigation right is uncapped in frequency and the notice undertaking is best-efforts only, but as it is a breach-remedy provision without any access to our environment we would leave it as drafted.

content.text:
**Finding: compliant — no redline proposed.**

The agreement contains no audit, inspection, verification or records-examination right running against Bluefly. Targeted searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "records", "monitor" and "premises" turned up nothing usable, and the sections that could plausibly host such a right (§ 4 charges/payment, § 11.5 Capacity Planning, § 12.1 License, §§ 13–14 general terms) contain none.

The planner's likely hook, § 11.3 Suspected Violations, is a breach-remedy provision only: IBM may investigate suspected breaches of the § 11.2(b) content warranties and then restrict access to the Services, require removal of Content, terminate, or pursue other remedies — with an undertaking to attempt notice before restricting access or removing Content. It gives IBM no access to our systems, personnel, books or records, and imposes no audit cost or cooperation burden on us.

That leaves us better off than the AUDIT preferred position (annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, vendor cost, no system access), so inserting an audit framework would only manufacture a right IBM does not have. I noted in the rationale, as a non-deviation observation, that § 11.3's investigation right is uncapped in frequency and its notice commitment is best-efforts only — acceptable given it carries no entry into our environment.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

paragraphs.text: 4.1 Charges

Charges for applicable Services will be specified in Service Option Attachments and Order Forms. Charges can be specified as one-time, installment, recurring, or usage. IBM will invoice such Charges when they begin or are due as set forth in Service Option Attachments.
11.5 Capacity Planning

Customer is responsible for determining whether the Base Components, IBM provided Internet access bandwidth, Customer Components and their combination will meet Customer's capacity or performance needs. Customer is responsible for planning for and requesting changes to the Base Components or IBM provided Internet access bandwidth, as determined by Customer, including any additional capacity required to support anticipated peaks in demand that may significantly increase Web site hits, transaction volumes, or otherwise increase system resource utilization.

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.

E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.

Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. input.quote: a. IBM will specify Materials to be delivered to Customer. IBM will identify them as being "Type I Materials," "Type II Materials," or otherwise as Customer and IBM agree in writing. If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials.
input.rationale: Section 7.0 defaults all Materials (deliverables) to Type II, i.e. IBM or third parties hold all right, title and interest, so work product created for us during the Service performance period is vendor-owned unless separately negotiated. The licence back for Type II Materials is limited to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform and distribute "within Customer's Enterprise only" — it carries no right to modify/prepare derivative works and no right to sublicense, so it fails the fallback position (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for our business) as well as the preferred position. There is also no affirmative statement that we retain all rights in our Content and Customer Components (Content is defined as customer-provided and Required Consents assumes third-party owners, but ownership is never confirmed). No assignment of our IP or data to IBM is created, so this is not walk-away territory. Redline flips the default to Type I (Customer-owned), broadens the Type II licence to include modification and sublicensing for our business, and adds a Customer Content/Customer Components ownership sentence; IBM's ownership of its pre-existing Materials and Base Components is left intact.

proposal.summary: Default Materials to Customer-owned Type I, broaden the Type II licence-back to include modification and sublicensing, and confirm Customer ownership of Content and Customer Components.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our playbook requires that we own the deliverables created for us, so we have made Type I (Customer-owned) the default where Materials are not otherwise specified, and confirmed that we retain all rights in our Content and Customer Components. Where IBM retains ownership of pre-existing Type II Materials, we need a perpetual licence that includes the right to modify and sublicense for our business purposes; retaining IBM ownership of its platform and generic tools is acceptable.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

input.quote: a. IBM will specify Materials to be delivered to Customer. IBM will identify them as being "Type I Materials," "Type II Materials," or otherwise as Customer and IBM agree in writing. If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials.
input.rationale: Section 7.0 defaults all Materials (deliverables) to Type II, i.e. IBM or third parties hold all right, title and interest, so work product created for us during the Service performance period is vendor-owned unless separately negotiated. The licence back for Type II Materials is limited to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform and distribute "within Customer's Enterprise only" — it carries no right to modify/prepare derivative works and no right to sublicense, so it fails the fallback position (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for our business) as well as the preferred position. There is also no affirmative statement that we retain all rights in our Content and Customer Components (Content is defined as customer-provided and Required Consents assumes third-party owners, but ownership is never confirmed). No assignment of our IP or data to IBM is created, so this is not walk-away territory. Redline flips the default to Type I (Customer-owned), broadens the Type II licence to include modification and sublicensing for our business, and adds a Customer Content/Customer Components ownership sentence; IBM's ownership of its pre-existing Materials and Base Components is left intact.

input.quote: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
input.rationale: Section 3.4(b) conditions Customer's termination for convenience on payment of "early termination charges" whose quantum is left entirely to Attachment A and the Service Option Attachments, with no cap in the Agreement. That is a Customer-payable liquidated amount on termination, so the rule applies (only Customer pays; there is no service-credit or Vendor-payable LD at issue). It fails both the preferred position (no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer) and the fallback (early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount), because the charge is open-ended and could reach or exceed the remaining contract value. The exposure is aggravated by Section 13.1, under which IBM may unilaterally change the terms of Attachment A on ninety days' notice, and there is no "sole remedy" language preventing IBM from also claiming damages. Section 3.3 helpfully disapplies these charges where IBM is in breach, and Section 9.2's liability cap does not limit termination charges, which are contract charges rather than damages. Because early termination charges are an embedded part of the priced facilities-services bargain, we proposed the fallback fix rather than outright deletion: a cap at three months' charges for the terminated Services, expressed as the sole amount payable and IBM's sole remedy for termination for convenience. Separately noted but not flagged here: Section 4.2's undefined "late payment fees" (a payment-terms point) and the Section 10 carve-out at p0123 for amounts for Services that would have been rendered but for Customer's breach (a consequential-damages point).

proposal.summary: Cap early termination charges at three months' charges and make them the sole termination amount payable by Customer
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We can accept an early termination charge, but it must be capped: our position is that no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by us, and at most an early-termination fee capped at three months' charges as the sole liquidated amount. As drafted the charge is open-ended and set in Attachment A, which IBM may change unilaterally under Section 13.1.

ops.oldText: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
ops.newText: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments, provided that such charges will not exceed, in the aggregate, three (3) months' charges for the terminated Services (calculated using the average monthly charges payable for such Services during the twelve (12) months preceding the notice date, or, if shorter, the period since the effective date) and will be the sole amount payable by Customer, and IBM's sole remedy, in respect of such termination for convenience.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.

Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.

Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

input.quote: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
input.rationale: Section 3.4(b) conditions Customer's termination for convenience on payment of "early termination charges" whose quantum is left entirely to Attachment A and the Service Option Attachments, with no cap in the Agreement. That is a Customer-payable liquidated amount on termination, so the rule applies (only Customer pays; there is no service-credit or Vendor-payable LD at issue). It fails both the preferred position (no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer) and the fallback (early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount), because the charge is open-ended and could reach or exceed the remaining contract value. The exposure is aggravated by Section 13.1, under which IBM may unilaterally change the terms of Attachment A on ninety days' notice, and there is no "sole remedy" language preventing IBM from also claiming damages. Section 3.3 helpfully disapplies these charges where IBM is in breach, and Section 9.2's liability cap does not limit termination charges, which are contract charges rather than damages. Because early termination charges are an embedded part of the priced facilities-services bargain, we proposed the fallback fix rather than outright deletion: a cap at three months' charges for the terminated Services, expressed as the sole amount payable and IBM's sole remedy for termination for convenience. Separately noted but not flagged here: Section 4.2's undefined "late payment fees" (a payment-terms point) and the Section 10 carve-out at p0123 for amounts for Services that would have been rendered but for Customer's breach (a consequential-damages point).

paragraphs.text: 3.4 Termination for Convenience

Customer may terminate this Agreement (including all Service Option Attachments) or any Service Option Attachment (with the exception of any Service Option Attachment that is a prerequisite for the provision of Services under a non-terminated Service Option Attachment) for convenience at the end of any calendar month by:
a. providing at least one month's prior written notice to IBM; and
b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
In the event that Customer exercises its rights under this Section 3.4, IBM shall continue to fulfill all of its duties and obligations following the notice date and until the final termination date.
3.1 Term

This Agreement will be effective beginning on 12:01 a.m., Eastern Time, on the day after the date of last signature to these Base Terms ("Effective Date") and ending on the expiration and/or termination of all Service Option Attachments, unless the Agreement is terminated earlier in accordance with the terms herein. The term of each Service Option Attachment is as specified on the applicable Order Form.
3.5 Effect of&sbsp;Termination

Upon the date of termination, all Customer payment obligations accrued hereunder through the date of termination will become due and payable. The termination of selected Service Option Attachments will not affect Customer's obligation to pay charges under other Service Option Attachments.

input.quote: a. it will perform the Services using reasonable care and skill and in accordance with the applicable Service Option Attachments
input.rationale: Section 5.1 gives a services performance warranty (reasonable care and skill, roughly equivalent to professional and workmanlike) and a compliance-with-laws covenant, but there is no conformance warranty for Deliverables/Materials, no warranty period, and no remedy anywhere in the agreement (no re-performance, repair, replacement or refund; no SLA or credits). Worse, Section 5.4(c) provides all Materials — including Type I Materials created for Customer — "AS IS" without warranty of any kind, so the disclaimer swallows any deliverable-level assurance. That fails even the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with the stated remedies) and approaches the walk-away position. Our redline sits at the fallback: a 90-day conformance warranty for Deliverables/Materials with a no-malicious-code assurance and an at-IBM's-option re-perform/repair/refund remedy, plus an "except as expressly warranted" carve-out in the AS IS disclaimer.

ops.text: c. for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable and the Materials will conform in all material respects to their applicable documentation and specifications, and the Materials will not contain any virus, worm or other malicious code. Customer's remedy for breach of the warranties in this Section 5.1 is, at IBM's option, re-performance of the non-conforming Services, repair or replacement of the non-conforming Deliverable or Materials, or a refund of the charges paid for the non-conforming Services, Deliverable or Materials.

ops.newText: c. Except as expressly warranted in Section 5.1, IBM PROVIDES ALL MATERIALS AND ALL NON-IBM SERVICES

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

You are an independent verifier of one proposed contract finding.
Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?
The claimed status matters: for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is expected, and you should pass when the cited text supports compliance. Fail a deviation finding whose cited clause already meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms (the playbook's classification semantics) — a redline that merely upgrades an acceptable fallback to preferred wording is over-flagging. Compliant findings are retained as internal evaluation evidence, not raised as negotiation issues. For deviation or missing findings, require an actionable valid proposal.
Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 7.0 defaults all Materials (deliverables) to Type II, i.e. IBM or third parties hold all right, title and interest, so work product created for us during the Service performance period is vendor-owned unless separately negotiated. The licence back for Type II Materials is limited to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform and distribute "within Customer's Enterprise only" — it carries no right to modify/prepare derivative works and no right to sublicense, so it fails the fallback position (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for our business) as well as the preferred position. There is also no affirmative statement that we retain all rights in our Content and Customer Components (Content is defined as customer-provided and Required Consents assumes third-party owners, but ownership is never confirmed). No assignment of our IP or data to IBM is created, so this is not walk-away territory. Redline flips the default to Type I (Customer-owned), broadens the Type II licence to include modification and sublicensing for our business, and adds a Customer Content/Customer Components ownership sentence; IBM's ownership of its pre-existing Materials and Base Components is left intact.

Original paragraphs:
p0082: a. IBM will specify Materials to be delivered to Customer. IBM will identify them as being "Type I Materials," "Type II Materials," or otherwise as Customer and IBM agree in writing. If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials.
p0085: c. Type II Materials are those, created during the Service performance period or otherwise (such as those that preexist the Service), in which IBM or third parties have all right, title, and interest (including ownership of copyright). IBM will deliver one copy of the specified Materials to Customer. IBM grants Customer an irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up license to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, and distribute, within Customer's Enterprise only, copies of Type II Materials.
p0086: d. The parties agree to reproduce the copyright notice and any other legend of ownership on any copies made under the licenses granted in this Section 7.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: Under this e-business Hosting Agreement ("Agreement") between International Business Machines Corporation ("IBM") and Bluefly, Inc. ("Customer"), IBM will provide Web hosting and related services ("Services") to Customer. The Agreement includes these terms and conditions and the documents referenced herein ("Base Terms"), e-business hosting services order forms accepted by IBM ("Order Forms"), and the following attachments:

Rendered redline:
p0082: a. IBM will specify Materials to be delivered to Customer. IBM will identify them as being "Type I Materials," "Type II Materials," or otherwise as Customer and IBM agree in writing. If not specified, Materials will be considered Type I Materials.
p0085: c. Type II Materials are those, created during the Service performance period or otherwise (such as those that preexist the Service), in which IBM or third parties have all right, title, and interest (including ownership of copyright). IBM will deliver one copy of the specified Materials to Customer. IBM grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up license to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, prepare derivative works based on, and distribute copies of Type II Materials for Customer's business purposes, and to sublicense these rights to its Affiliates, Subcontractors and Services Recipients.
p0086: d. The parties agree to reproduce the copyright notice and any other legend of ownership on any copies made under the licenses granted in this Section 7.
e. Customer retains all right, title, and interest (including all intellectual property rights) in and to the Content and the Customer Components. Nothing in this Agreement assigns or transfers to IBM any ownership of the Content or the Customer Components, and IBM obtains no rights in them other than the limited rights expressly granted in this Agreement for the purpose of performing the Services.

Comment:
[Playbook] Our playbook requires that we own the deliverables created for us, so we have made Type I (Customer-owned) the default where Materials are not otherwise specified, and confirmed that we retain all rights in our Content and Customer Components. Where IBM retains ownership of pre-existing Type II Materials, we need a perpetual licence that includes the right to modify and sublicense for our business purposes; retaining IBM ownership of its platform and generic tools is acceptable.

**Finding: deviation (Section 3.4(b), p0046)** — validated redline submitted.

**What I found.** The document contains no "liquidated damages" language and no service-credit regime (§11.1 is a Customer support obligation, not credits). The single Customer-payable liquidated amount is §3.4(b): termination for convenience requires "paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments."

**Why it fails the fallback.** The charge is uncapped in the Agreement — quantum is deferred entirely to Attachment A, which is not in the body and which IBM may unilaterally amend on 90 days' notice under §13.1. So the amount could reach or exceed remaining contract value (walk-away territory), and there is no "sole remedy" language stopping IBM from claiming damages on top. §9.2's liability cap does not help, since termination charges are contract charges rather than damages.

**Mitigating point noted:** §3.3 already disapplies these charges where IBM is the breaching party — that carve-out is in our favour and I left it alone.

**Fix applied at the fallback, not preferred.** Because early termination charges are embedded in the priced facilities-services bargain, outright deletion would be disproportionate. The edit caps them at three months' charges for the terminated Services and makes them the sole amount payable and IBM's sole remedy.

**Adjacent issues flagged in the rationale but deliberately not redlined here** (to avoid double-flagging the same commercial term under two rules):
- §4.2's undefined "late payment fees" — a payment-terms point.
- §10's carve-out at p0123 for "amounts owing for Services that would have been rendered but for Customer's breach," which functions as lost-revenue recovery against us — a consequential-damages point worth checking under that rule.

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.
Detection guidance:
Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 3.4(b) conditions Customer's termination for convenience on payment of "early termination charges" whose quantum is left entirely to Attachment A and the Service Option Attachments, with no cap in the Agreement. That is a Customer-payable liquidated amount on termination, so the rule applies (only Customer pays; there is no service-credit or Vendor-payable LD at issue). It fails both the preferred position (no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer) and the fallback (early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount), because the charge is open-ended and could reach or exceed the remaining contract value. The exposure is aggravated by Section 13.1, under which IBM may unilaterally change the terms of Attachment A on ninety days' notice, and there is no "sole remedy" language preventing IBM from also claiming damages. Section 3.3 helpfully disapplies these charges where IBM is in breach, and Section 9.2's liability cap does not limit termination charges, which are contract charges rather than damages. Because early termination charges are an embedded part of the priced facilities-services bargain, we proposed the fallback fix rather than outright deletion: a cap at three months' charges for the terminated Services, expressed as the sole amount payable and IBM's sole remedy for termination for convenience. Separately noted but not flagged here: Section 4.2's undefined "late payment fees" (a payment-terms point) and the Section 10 carve-out at p0123 for amounts for Services that would have been rendered but for Customer's breach (a consequential-damages point).

Original paragraphs:
p0046: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.

Resolved definitions:

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 5.1 gives a services performance warranty (reasonable care and skill, roughly equivalent to professional and workmanlike) and a compliance-with-laws covenant, but there is no conformance warranty for Deliverables/Materials, no warranty period, and no remedy anywhere in the agreement (no re-performance, repair, replacement or refund; no SLA or credits). Worse, Section 5.4(c) provides all Materials — including Type I Materials created for Customer — "AS IS" without warranty of any kind, so the disclaimer swallows any deliverable-level assurance. That fails even the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with the stated remedies) and approaches the walk-away position. Our redline sits at the fallback: a 90-day conformance warranty for Deliverables/Materials with a no-malicious-code assurance and an at-IBM's-option re-perform/repair/refund remedy, plus an "except as expressly warranted" carve-out in the AS IS disclaimer.

Original paragraphs:
p0061: a. it will perform the Services using reasonable care and skill and in accordance with the applicable Service Option Attachments (which means the degree of knowledge, skill and judgment customarily exercised by members of the applicable profession with respect to work of a similar nature); and that it will provide Customer with competent, fully trained, fully qualified and responsible personnel to perform the Services; and
p0062: b. it has the requisite corporate power and authority to execute, deliver and perform its obligations under this Agreement.
p0074: c. IBM PROVIDES ALL MATERIALS AND ALL NON-IBM SERVICES, PRODUCTS, DATA, APPARATUS AND SOFTWARE "AS IS", WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, INCLUDING, WITHOUT LIMITATION, THE IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, SATISFACTORY QUALITY, AND FITNESS FOR&sbsp;A PARTICULAR PURPOSE. Non-IBM suppliers may provide their own warranties to you.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: Under this e-business Hosting Agreement ("Agreement") between International Business Machines Corporation ("IBM") and Bluefly, Inc. ("Customer"), IBM will provide Web hosting and related services ("Services") to Customer. The Agreement includes these terms and conditions and the documents referenced herein ("Base Terms"), e-business hosting services order forms accepted by IBM ("Order Forms"), and the following attachments:
Service Option Attachments: c. all other applicable attachments referenced in the Order Forms for Services options selected by Customer ("Service Option Attachments").

Rendered redline:
p0062: b. it has the requisite corporate power and authority to execute, deliver and perform its obligations under this Agreement.
c. for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable and the Materials will conform in all material respects to their applicable documentation and specifications, and the Materials will not contain any virus, worm or other malicious code. Customer's remedy for breach of the warranties in this Section 5.1 is, at IBM's option, re-performance of the non-conforming Services, repair or replacement of the non-conforming Deliverable or Materials, or a refund of the charges paid for the non-conforming Services, Deliverable or Materials.
p0074: c. Except as expressly warranted in Section 5.1, IBM PROVIDES ALL MATERIALS AND ALL NON-IBM SERVICES, PRODUCTS, DATA, APPARATUS AND SOFTWARE "AS IS", WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, INCLUDING, WITHOUT LIMITATION, THE IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, SATISFACTORY QUALITY, AND FITNESS FOR&sbsp;A PARTICULAR PURPOSE. Non-IBM suppliers may provide their own warranties to you.

Comment:
[Playbook] We have added a 90-day conformance warranty for Deliverables and Materials with a re-performance/repair/refund remedy, plus a no-malicious-code assurance, and carved the express warranties out of the "AS IS" disclaimer so it does not swallow them. Our playbook requires a real conformance warranty and remedy; 90 days is our fallback position, and we are happy to discuss the mechanics.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.

Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
No audit right binds the Customer anywhere in this Agreement, so our position is better than the AUDIT preferred position and the clause set is compliant with no redline.

Evidence: searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "monitor" and "premises" return no hits; "records" appears only in the § 9.1 liability carve-out for loss of records or data. The sections that could host a usage-verification right contain none — § 4.1 Charges / § 4.2 Payment, § 11.5 Capacity Planning (allocates capacity-planning responsibility to Customer only), § 12.1 License (copying/reverse-engineering restrictions only), § 13.2 Acceptable Use Policy (IBM modification right on 30 days' notice) and §§ 14.1–14.20.

The planner's candidate hook, § 11.3, is a breach-remedy provision, not an audit right: IBM may investigate suspected breaches of the § 11.2(b) content/acceptable-use warranties and then restrict access to the Services, require removal of Content, terminate for cause or pursue other remedies (p0132–p0136), with an undertaking to attempt notice before restricting access or removing Content (p0137). It confers no right of access to Bluefly's systems, personnel, books or records, no remote access, and no audit cost or cooperation burden on us. There is therefore nothing to parametrize with frequency, notice, independent-auditor, cost-shifting or no-system-access limits.

Inapplicable deterministic check: the "audit frequency limited" test fails only because no audit clause exists to carry a frequency cap. That is an artifact of absence, not a material failure — the walk-away triggers (unlimited or unannounced audits, remote access to Customer systems) are not met because no audit or access right is granted at all. Inserting frequency/notice/cost language would manufacture an audit right in IBM's favour that it does not currently hold, contrary to our interest as customer.

Residual observation, noted rather than flagged: § 11.3's investigation right is uncapped in frequency and its notice commitment is best-efforts ("will attempt to notify") with emergency and legal-requirement carve-outs. As a minor sub-element of a remedy clause that involves no entry into our environment, we would leave it as drafted; if § 11.3 is later expanded to include access to Customer records or systems, this rule should be re-run against it.

Original paragraphs:
p0132: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b). If IBM reasonably determines that a breach of any such warranty has occurred, then IBM may, in its sole and reasonable discretion:
p0133: a. restrict Customer's access to the Services;
p0137: Except in an emergency or as may otherwise be required by law, before undertaking the activities in Subsection 11.3(a) or 11.3(b), IBM will attempt to notify Customer by any reasonably practical means under the circumstances, such as, without limitation, by telephone or e-mail.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: Under this e-business Hosting Agreement ("Agreement") between International Business Machines Corporation ("IBM") and Bluefly, Inc. ("Customer"), IBM will provide Web hosting and related services ("Services") to Customer. The Agreement includes these terms and conditions and the documents referenced herein ("Base Terms"), e-business hosting services order forms accepted by IBM ("Order Forms"), and the following attachments:

Rendered redline:
p0132: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b). If IBM reasonably determines that a breach of any such warranty has occurred, then IBM may, in its sole and reasonable discretion:
p0133: a. restrict Customer's access to the Services;
p0137: Except in an emergency or as may otherwise be required by law, before undertaking the activities in Subsection 11.3(a) or 11.3(b), IBM will attempt to notify Customer by any reasonably practical means under the circumstances, such as, without limitation, by telephone or e-mail.

Comment:
none

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.quote: Risk of loss for all Base Components shall at all times remain with IBM. Risk of loss for all Customer Components shall at all times remain with Customer.
input.rationale: The agreement contains no insurance clause: the section outline has no insurance heading, and searches for "insur" return no hits anywhere in the document (Section 14.12 Risk of Loss and Section 5.3 Security are the nearest neighbours and address allocation of risk and security features only, not coverage). IBM is a hosting provider operating the e-business Hosting Environment and holding Customer Components, so the absence of any insurance obligation sits in walk-away territory under the rule (no insurance for a vendor that processes our data). We therefore insert a short insurance section after Section 14.12 at the preferred position (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request), with the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback flagged in the comment.

ops.text: Insurance

IBM shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: (a) commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; (b) professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; (c) where IBM hosts, stores or otherwise processes Customer Components or other Customer data, cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000; and (d) workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law. IBM shall provide certificates of insurance evidencing such coverage upon Customer's request.

E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.

No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.

Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

content.text: These Base Terms contain no minimum purchase commitment. Charges are tied to ordered Services and usage, and Customer holds a broad convenience exit. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: Charges for applicable Services will be specified in Service Option Attachments and Order Forms. Charges can be specified as one-time, installment, recurring, or usage. IBM will invoice such Charges when they begin or are due as set forth in Service Option Attachments.
input.rationale: The Base Terms impose no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, committed volume or shortfall charge on Customer, which meets the preferred position. Searches for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall", "purchase" and "volume" return nothing of the kind: § 4.1 (p0052) prices only ordered Services on a one-time, installment, recurring or usage basis, and § 11.5 Capacity Planning (p0142) allocates capacity forecasting responsibility to Customer without any floor or cap on Customer usage — it lets Customer request changes "as determined by Customer," which is a discretion in our favour rather than a commitment. Customer also has an unconditional exit under § 3.4: termination for convenience of the Agreement or any Service Option Attachment at the end of any calendar month on one month's notice (p0044–p0045), which is more generous than the fallback's 30-day reduction right, and § 3.3 confirms IBM cannot recover early termination charges where IBM has breached. Two diligence notes, not deviations: (i) § 3.4(b) (p0046) conditions the convenience exit on "the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments," and (ii) § 3.5 (p0049) preserves charges under non-terminated Service Option Attachments. Those attachments and Order Forms are not part of the text under review, so any committed spend, minimum volume or termination-charge formula must be checked there when the commercial schedules are issued; the mechanics in the Base Terms themselves are compliant. No redline proposed.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.

Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.

"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
