input.rationale: The Agreement grants IBM no audit, inspection, verification or usage-examination right against Bluefly: searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "records", "monitor" and "premises" return nothing relevant, and no such right appears in §§ 4 (Charges/Payment), 11 (IBM obligations/Suspected Violations), 12 (License) or 13-14. The closest hook, § 11.3, is only a right for IBM to investigate suspected breaches of the Customer content/acceptable-use warranties and to restrict access, remove Content or terminate, coupled with an attempt-to-notify commitment (p0137); it confers no access to Bluefly's systems, personnel, books or records and imposes no audit cost or cooperation burden on us. Because there is no audit right binding the Customer, the position is better than the preferred position (annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Vendor cost, no system access), so nothing needs to be inserted or limited — adding an audit framework would only create a right IBM does not currently have. Residual note (not a deviation): § 11.3's investigation right is uncapped in frequency and the notice undertaking is best-efforts only, but as it is a breach-remedy provision without any access to our environment we would leave it as drafted.

input.rationale:
No audit right binds the Customer anywhere in this Agreement, so our position is better than the AUDIT preferred position and the clause set is compliant with no redline.

Evidence: searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "monitor" and "premises" return no hits; "records" appears only in the § 9.1 liability carve-out for loss of records or data. The sections that could host a usage-verification right contain none — § 4.1 Charges / § 4.2 Payment, § 11.5 Capacity Planning (allocates capacity-planning responsibility to Customer only), § 12.1 License (copying/reverse-engineering restrictions only), § 13.2 Acceptable Use Policy (IBM modification right on 30 days' notice) and §§ 14.1–14.20.

The planner's candidate hook, § 11.3, is a breach-remedy provision, not an audit right: IBM may investigate suspected breaches of the § 11.2(b) content/acceptable-use warranties and then restrict access to the Services, require removal of Content, terminate for cause or pursue other remedies (p0132–p0136), with an undertaking to attempt notice before restricting access or removing Content (p0137). It confers no right of access to Bluefly's systems, personnel, books or records, no remote access, and no audit cost or cooperation burden on us. There is therefore nothing to parametrize with frequency, notice, independent-auditor, cost-shifting or no-system-access limits.

Inapplicable deterministic check: the "audit frequency limited" test fails only because no audit clause exists to carry a frequency cap. That is an artifact of absence, not a material failure — the walk-away triggers (unlimited or unannounced audits, remote access to Customer systems) are not met because no audit or access right is granted at all. Inserting frequency/notice/cost language would manufacture an audit right in IBM's favour that it does not currently hold, contrary to our interest as customer.

Residual observation, noted rather than flagged: § 11.3's investigation right is uncapped in frequency and its notice commitment is best-efforts ("will attempt to notify") with emergency and legal-requirement carve-outs. As a minor sub-element of a remedy clause that involves no entry into our environment, we would leave it as drafted; if § 11.3 is later expanded to include access to Customer records or systems, this rule should be re-run against it.

paragraphs.text: 14.18 Data Protection

You agree to allow International Business Machines Corporation and entities within its Enterprise to store and use your contact information, including names, phone numbers, and e-mail addresses, anywhere they do business. Such information will be processed and used in connection with our business relationship, and may be provided to contractors, Business Partners, and assignees of IBM Corp. and entities within its Enterprise for uses consistent with their collective business activities, including communicating with you (for example, for processing orders, for promotions, and for marketing research). For personal information processed by IBM on your behalf as part of the Services, IBM will act in accordance with your instructions by following such processing and security obligations as are contained in this Agreement. You also confirm that you are solely responsible for ensuring that any processing and security obligations comply with applicable data protection laws. Your contact information shall not be considered personal information processed on your behalf.
14.2 Survival

Any of these terms and conditions which by their nature extend beyond the Agreement termination or expiration remain in effect until fulfilled, including, without limitation, Sections 3.5, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11.2, 11.3, 11.6, 12.2, 12.3, and 14, and apply to both Customer's and IBM's respective successors and assignees.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

**Finding: missing (insurance clause absent)**

The agreement has no insurance provision anywhere — no insurance heading in the outline and zero text hits for "insur". The nearest neighbours only allocate risk of loss (§14.12) and describe security features with heavy disclaimers (§5.3). Since IBM hosts our environment and holds Customer Components, having no insurance obligation is walk-away territory under the rule.

Redline (validated, ok:true): a new §14.12A "Insurance" inserted after §14.12 at the preferred position — CGL USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M where IBM processes our data, workers' compensation as required by law, and certificates on request — with the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback offered in the comment.

You are an independent verifier of one proposed contract finding.
Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?
The claimed status matters: for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is expected, and you should pass when the cited text supports compliance. Fail a deviation finding whose cited clause already meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms (the playbook's classification semantics) — a redline that merely upgrades an acceptable fallback to preferred wording is over-flagging. Compliant findings are retained as internal evaluation evidence, not raised as negotiation issues. For deviation or missing findings, require an actionable valid proposal.
Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.


Claimed finding status: missing

Finding rationale:
The agreement contains no insurance clause: the section outline has no insurance heading, and searches for "insur" return no hits anywhere in the document (Section 14.12 Risk of Loss and Section 5.3 Security are the nearest neighbours and address allocation of risk and security features only, not coverage). IBM is a hosting provider operating the e-business Hosting Environment and holding Customer Components, so the absence of any insurance obligation sits in walk-away territory under the rule (no insurance for a vendor that processes our data). We therefore insert a short insurance section after Section 14.12 at the preferred position (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request), with the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback flagged in the comment.

Original paragraphs:
p0192: Risk of loss for all Base Components shall at all times remain with IBM. Risk of loss for all Customer Components shall at all times remain with Customer.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: Under this e-business Hosting Agreement ("Agreement") between International Business Machines Corporation ("IBM") and Bluefly, Inc. ("Customer"), IBM will provide Web hosting and related services ("Services") to Customer. The Agreement includes these terms and conditions and the documents referenced herein ("Base Terms"), e-business hosting services order forms accepted by IBM ("Order Forms"), and the following attachments:

Rendered redline:
p0192: Risk of loss for all Base Components shall at all times remain with IBM. Risk of loss for all Customer Components shall at all times remain with Customer.
Insurance
IBM shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: (a) commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; (b) professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; (c) where IBM hosts, stores or otherwise processes Customer Components or other Customer data, cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000; and (d) workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law. IBM shall provide certificates of insurance evidencing such coverage upon Customer's request.

Comment:
[Playbook] We have added a short insurance section, as the agreement currently has none even though IBM hosts our environment and processes our data. Our playbook position is CGL of USD 1M/2M, professional liability of USD 2M and cyber liability of USD 5M with certificates on request; we can discuss E&O of USD 1M and cyber of USD 2M as a fallback.

content.text: {"verdict":"pass","reasons":["Deviation classification is correct: Section 5.1 contains only a services standard-of-care and corporate-authority warranty with no conformance warranty for Deliverables/Materials, no warranty period and no stated remedy, and the broad 'AS IS' disclaimer at p0074 covers all Materials — this fails the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with repair, replace, re-perform or refund) and edges toward walk-away.","Redline is actionable and directionally correct: it inserts a 90-day conformance warranty for Deliverables/Materials with a no-malicious-code assurance and an at-IBM's-option re-perform/repair/refund remedy, and adds an 'Except as expressly warranted in Section 5.1' carve-out so the disclaimer does not swallow the express warranty — exactly the rule's redline guidance.","The failed 'warranty period ≥ 90 days' regex is a false negative: the inserted text expressly states 'for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery'. The 0.46 changed-character ratio on p0074 is explained by the necessary prefatory carve-out; the disclaimer's substance is otherwise preserved.","Comment is accurate, concise, in our voice, cites the playbook and correctly identifies 90 days as the fallback while inviting discussion.","Minor, non-blocking nits: the rationale asserts a compliance-with-laws covenant that is not visible in the cited paragraphs, and the new clause 'c.' follows a subsection 'b.' ending in a period, so the list conjunction may need tidying on execution."]}

The Base Terms sit at the **preferred** position for MINCOMMIT:

- **No commitment mechanic exists.** Searches for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall", "take or pay", "purchase" and "volume" surface nothing relevant. § 4.1 charges only for ordered Services on a one-time, installment, recurring or usage basis.

- **Exit right exceeds the fallback.** § 3.4 gives Customer convenience termination of the Agreement or any single Service Option Attachment at the end of any calendar month on one month's notice; § 3.3 bars IBM from recovering early termination charges where IBM has breached.

Two diligence notes recorded in the rationale rather than flagged as deviations, since both live outside the text under review:

2. § 3.5 preserves charges under non-terminated Service Option Attachments.

Any committed spend, minimum volume, or penalty-style termination-charge formula would have to appear in those attachments or Order Forms. Worth re-running this rule against the commercial schedules when issued — if a shortfall penalty shows up there, the redline guidance (narrow to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, true-up instead of penalty) would apply at that point.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
The Base Terms impose no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, committed volume or shortfall charge on Customer, which meets the preferred position. Searches for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall", "purchase" and "volume" return nothing of the kind: § 4.1 (p0052) prices only ordered Services on a one-time, installment, recurring or usage basis, and § 11.5 Capacity Planning (p0142) allocates capacity forecasting responsibility to Customer without any floor or cap on Customer usage — it lets Customer request changes "as determined by Customer," which is a discretion in our favour rather than a commitment. Customer also has an unconditional exit under § 3.4: termination for convenience of the Agreement or any Service Option Attachment at the end of any calendar month on one month's notice (p0044–p0045), which is more generous than the fallback's 30-day reduction right, and § 3.3 confirms IBM cannot recover early termination charges where IBM has breached. Two diligence notes, not deviations: (i) § 3.4(b) (p0046) conditions the convenience exit on "the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments," and (ii) § 3.5 (p0049) preserves charges under non-terminated Service Option Attachments. Those attachments and Order Forms are not part of the text under review, so any committed spend, minimum volume or termination-charge formula must be checked there when the commercial schedules are issued; the mechanics in the Base Terms themselves are compliant. No redline proposed.

Original paragraphs:
p0052: Charges for applicable Services will be specified in Service Option Attachments and Order Forms. Charges can be specified as one-time, installment, recurring, or usage. IBM will invoice such Charges when they begin or are due as set forth in Service Option Attachments.
p0044: Customer may terminate this Agreement (including all Service Option Attachments) or any Service Option Attachment (with the exception of any Service Option Attachment that is a prerequisite for the provision of Services under a non-terminated Service Option Attachment) for convenience at the end of any calendar month by:
p0045: a. providing at least one month's prior written notice to IBM; and
p0046: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
p0142: Customer is responsible for determining whether the Base Components, IBM provided Internet access bandwidth, Customer Components and their combination will meet Customer's capacity or performance needs. Customer is responsible for planning for and requesting changes to the Base Components or IBM provided Internet access bandwidth, as determined by Customer, including any additional capacity required to support anticipated peaks in demand that may significantly increase Web site hits, transaction volumes, or otherwise increase system resource utilization.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: Under this e-business Hosting Agreement ("Agreement") between International Business Machines Corporation ("IBM") and Bluefly, Inc. ("Customer"), IBM will provide Web hosting and related services ("Services") to Customer. The Agreement includes these terms and conditions and the documents referenced herein ("Base Terms"), e-business hosting services order forms accepted by IBM ("Order Forms"), and the following attachments:
Order Forms: Under this e-business Hosting Agreement ("Agreement") between International Business Machines Corporation ("IBM") and Bluefly, Inc. ("Customer"), IBM will provide Web hosting and related services ("Services") to Customer. The Agreement includes these terms and conditions and the documents referenced herein ("Base Terms"), e-business hosting services order forms accepted by IBM ("Order Forms"), and the following attachments:
Service Option Attachments: c. all other applicable attachments referenced in the Order Forms for Services options selected by Customer ("Service Option Attachments").

Rendered redline:
p0052: Charges for applicable Services will be specified in Service Option Attachments and Order Forms. Charges can be specified as one-time, installment, recurring, or usage. IBM will invoice such Charges when they begin or are due as set forth in Service Option Attachments.
p0044: Customer may terminate this Agreement (including all Service Option Attachments) or any Service Option Attachment (with the exception of any Service Option Attachment that is a prerequisite for the provision of Services under a non-terminated Service Option Attachment) for convenience at the end of any calendar month by:
p0045: a. providing at least one month's prior written notice to IBM; and
p0046: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
p0142: Customer is responsible for determining whether the Base Components, IBM provided Internet access bandwidth, Customer Components and their combination will meet Customer's capacity or performance needs. Customer is responsible for planning for and requesting changes to the Base Components or IBM provided Internet access bandwidth, as determined by Customer, including any additional capacity required to support anticipated peaks in demand that may significantly increase Web site hits, transaction volumes, or otherwise increase system resource utilization.

none

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

content.text: The verifier's substantive checks all pass and confirm the compliant call; the only failing item remains the deterministic "audit frequency limited" test, which the verifier itself characterizes as an artifact of there being no audit clause to parametrize. There is no material defect left to repair, so I'll submit a final, tightened version of the same finding — still with no redline and no comment, as required for a compliant finding.

input.quote: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b). If IBM reasonably determines that a breach of any such warranty has occurred, then IBM may, in its sole and reasonable discretion:
input.rationale:
Compliant: no audit, inspection or verification right binds the Customer anywhere in this Agreement, which puts us better than the AUDIT preferred position. No redline or comment is proposed.

Evidence of absence: searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "monitor" and "premises" return no hits; "records" appears only in the § 9.1 liability carve-out for loss of records or data. Sections that could host a usage-verification right contain none — § 4.1 Charges, § 4.2 Payment, § 11.5 Capacity Planning, § 12.1 License, § 13.2 Acceptable Use Policy and §§ 14.1–14.20.

The planner's candidate hook, § 11.3, is a breach-investigation and remedy provision rather than an audit right: IBM may investigate suspected breaches of the § 11.2(b) content/acceptable-use warranties and then restrict access to the Services, require removal of Content, terminate for cause or pursue other remedies (p0132–p0136), with an undertaking to attempt notice first (p0137). It grants no access to Bluefly's premises, systems, personnel, books or records, no remote access, and imposes no audit cost or cooperation burden. There is accordingly nothing to parametrize with frequency, notice, independent-auditor, cost-shifting or no-system-access limits, and no walk-away trigger (unlimited or unannounced audits, remote access to Customer systems) is present.

The failing "audit frequency limited" deterministic check is an artifact of that absence, not a material failure. Treating this as "missing" and inserting frequency/notice/cost limits would manufacture a verification right in IBM's favour that it does not hold, contrary to the rule's protective purpose and the instruction not to flag terms that benefit our party.

Residual observation, noted rather than escalated per the minor sub-element rule: § 11.3's investigation right is uncapped in frequency and its notice commitment is best-efforts ("will attempt to notify") with emergency and legal-requirement carve-outs. We would leave it as drafted; if § 11.3 is later expanded to reach Customer records or systems, this rule should be re-run against it.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.

Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.

content.text:
**Final finding: compliant — no redline, no comment.**

This is my last call on this rule; the position is settled and I'm not making further changes.

**Why compliant.** IBM holds no audit, inspection, verification or record/system-access right over Bluefly anywhere in the agreement. Searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "monitor" and "premises" return nothing; "records" appears only in the § 9.1 liability carve-out. Every section that could plausibly host a usage-verification right — §§ 4.1, 4.2, 11.5, 12.1, 13.2 and 14.1–14.20 — contains none.

**§ 11.3 is not an audit hook.** It is a breach-investigation and remedy provision tied to the § 11.2(b) content/acceptable-use warranties: IBM may investigate, then restrict Service access, require Content removal, terminate for cause or pursue other remedies, with a best-efforts notice undertaking. It confers no access to our premises, systems, personnel, books or records and imposes no audit cost or cooperation burden.

**On the failing deterministic check.** "Audit frequency limited" fails only because there is no audit clause to carry a frequency cap — an artifact of absence, which the verifier's own reasoning confirms. No walk-away trigger is present, since neither an audit right nor system access is granted. Repairing this check by inserting frequency, notice or cost limits would manufacture a verification right in IBM's favour that the contract does not currently give it, contrary to the rule's protective purpose and the instruction not to flag terms favourable to us. That is the one change I have declined to make across all three passes.

**Carried forward for the negotiation file:** § 11.3's investigation right is uncapped in frequency and its notice commitment is best-efforts with emergency and legal-requirement carve-outs — acceptable as drafted, but this rule should be re-run if § 11.3 is ever expanded to reach our records or systems.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Compliant: no audit, inspection or verification right binds the Customer anywhere in this Agreement, which puts us better than the AUDIT preferred position. No redline or comment is proposed.

Evidence of absence: searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "monitor" and "premises" return no hits; "records" appears only in the § 9.1 liability carve-out for loss of records or data. Sections that could host a usage-verification right contain none — § 4.1 Charges, § 4.2 Payment, § 11.5 Capacity Planning, § 12.1 License, § 13.2 Acceptable Use Policy and §§ 14.1–14.20.

The planner's candidate hook, § 11.3, is a breach-investigation and remedy provision rather than an audit right: IBM may investigate suspected breaches of the § 11.2(b) content/acceptable-use warranties and then restrict access to the Services, require removal of Content, terminate for cause or pursue other remedies (p0132–p0136), with an undertaking to attempt notice first (p0137). It grants no access to Bluefly's premises, systems, personnel, books or records, no remote access, and imposes no audit cost or cooperation burden. There is accordingly nothing to parametrize with frequency, notice, independent-auditor, cost-shifting or no-system-access limits, and no walk-away trigger (unlimited or unannounced audits, remote access to Customer systems) is present.

The failing "audit frequency limited" deterministic check is an artifact of that absence, not a material failure. Treating this as "missing" and inserting frequency/notice/cost limits would manufacture a verification right in IBM's favour that it does not hold, contrary to the rule's protective purpose and the instruction not to flag terms that benefit our party.

Residual observation, noted rather than escalated per the minor sub-element rule: § 11.3's investigation right is uncapped in frequency and its notice commitment is best-efforts ("will attempt to notify") with emergency and legal-requirement carve-outs. We would leave it as drafted; if § 11.3 is later expanded to reach Customer records or systems, this rule should be re-run against it.

**Finding: missing** (TRANSITION) — inserted a transition-assistance and data-return clause into § 3.5.

- **What's there:** § 3.5 Effect of Termination only accelerates Customer's payment obligations. Nothing else in the agreement addresses exit: searches for "transition", "return", "export" and "delet" turn up nothing relevant; § 14.18 covers only contact information, and § 11.6 places responsibility for Content on us without any return mechanic.
- **Why it fails:** The agreement is a hosting agreement where our Content sits in IBM's e-business Hosting Environment, yet there is no obligation to return or export it, and no wind-down period — below the fallback (90 days' assistance plus 30-day export).
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** New paragraph in § 3.5 requiring (a) up to six months' transition assistance at IBM's then-current rates, (b) return/export of all Content in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and (c) deletion with written certification. Drafted using the defined term "Content" for consistency, and § 14.2 already lists § 3.5 as surviving termination.

You are an independent verifier of one proposed contract finding.
Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?
The claimed status matters: for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is expected, and you should pass when the cited text supports compliance. Fail a deviation finding whose cited clause already meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms (the playbook's classification semantics) — a redline that merely upgrades an acceptable fallback to preferred wording is over-flagging. Compliant findings are retained as internal evaluation evidence, not raised as negotiation issues. For deviation or missing findings, require an actionable valid proposal.
Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Claimed finding status: missing

Finding rationale:
Section 3.5 (Effect of Termination) addresses only Customer's payment obligations; searches for "transition", "return", "export" and "delet" show no exit assistance, data return/export or deletion obligations anywhere in this hosting agreement (14.18 Data Protection covers only contact information, and 11.6 makes Customer responsible for Content without any return mechanic). With no obligation to return Content, this falls short of even the fallback (90 days' assistance plus 30-day export), so we insert the preferred exit clause into § 3.5, which is already carried forward by the § 14.2 survival list.

Original paragraphs:
p0049: Upon the date of termination, all Customer payment obligations accrued hereunder through the date of termination will become due and payable. The termination of selected Service Option Attachments will not affect Customer's obligation to pay charges under other Service Option Attachments.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: Under this e-business Hosting Agreement ("Agreement") between International Business Machines Corporation ("IBM") and Bluefly, Inc. ("Customer"), IBM will provide Web hosting and related services ("Services") to Customer. The Agreement includes these terms and conditions and the documents referenced herein ("Base Terms"), e-business hosting services order forms accepted by IBM ("Order Forms"), and the following attachments:
Service Option Attachments: c. all other applicable attachments referenced in the Order Forms for Services options selected by Customer ("Service Option Attachments").

Rendered redline:
p0049: Upon the date of termination, all Customer payment obligations accrued hereunder through the date of termination will become due and payable. The termination of selected Service Option Attachments will not affect Customer's obligation to pay charges under other Service Option Attachments.
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, IBM shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at IBM's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of Customer's request, return or make available for export all Content in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Content from its systems and certify such deletion to Customer in writing.

Comment:
[Playbook] We have added a standard exit clause to Section 3.5 so that, on termination, IBM provides up to six months of paid transition assistance and returns our Content in a machine-readable format within 30 days before deleting it and certifying deletion. The Agreement is currently silent on data return and wind-down, which would leave our hosted data stranded; we can accept a 90-day assistance period as a fallback.

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — IBM e-business Hosting Agreement (Base Terms)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Verified playbook findings — hosting agreement Base Terms 

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Base Terms against the playbook and confirmed 18 findings: 2 critical deviations, 4 high-severity deviations (with 2 high-severity items compliant), 5 medium-severity deviations or gaps, 1 low-severity gap, 3 medium-severity compliant items, and 2 items recorded as needs_review for internal confirmation only.

The commercial core of the risk is concentrated in four places. First, indemnity: IBM's IP indemnity in § 8.1 sits acceptably at our fallback, but § 8.2(a)(3) requires **us** to indemnify IBM for any Services Recipient claim "related, directly or indirectly, to the Services," leaving us exposed for IBM's own ordinary negligence and service defects — walk-away territory. Second, liability: the § 9 cap is mutual and adequately sized, but the only carve-outs are indemnification payments and bodily injury/tangible property; confidentiality and data breaches are affirmatively capped because § 6 makes §§ 9 and 10 prevail over the confidentiality agreement. Third, exit economics: both § 3.4(b) (termination for convenience) and § 3.2 (renewal) are open-ended — uncapped early termination charges set in Attachment A, which IBM may unilaterally change on 90 days' notice under § 13.1, and auto-renewal for a term equal to the prior term with a 90-day notice window. Fourth, the deliverable and assurance package: Materials default to vendor-owned Type II with a narrow licence back, § 5.4(c) delivers all Materials "AS IS" with no warranty remedy anywhere, there is no transition assistance or Content return obligation, and there is no insurance clause at all.

On the positive side, we confirmed no exclusivity, no non-compete, no MFN, no minimum purchase commitment, no non-solicitation binding us, and no audit right against us; governing law is New York (our preferred position) with no arbitration or foreign venue. Our convenience-termination notice (one month) and IBM's lack of any convenience right are better than our fallback and should be preserved.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 8.1 Indemnification by IBM | § 8.1 sits at our fallback (IP-only, capped credit) and is not redlined; § 8.2(a)(3) forces a one-way Customer indemnity for claims related directly or indirectly to IBM's own Services, with § 8.2(c) relief only for IBM's bad faith, wilful misconduct, gross negligence or breach. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 9.1 IBM's Limitation of Liability | Cap basis, mutuality and the § 10 consequential-damages exclusion meet or exceed fallback; carve-outs are limited to indemnification payments and bodily injury/tangible property, with no carve-out for confidentiality, data protection, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud or IP infringement. |
| High | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 5.4 Other Disclaimers | § 7.0 defaults all Materials to Type II (vendor-owned); the licence back is enterprise-use only with no modification or sublicensing right, and Customer ownership of Content and Customer Components is never confirmed. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 12.1 License | Grant is expressly "revocable" with no standard for revocation (walk-away), and runs to Customer alone — Affiliates and our contractors are excluded, reinforced by § 14.17. Successor transfer is covered by § 14.10. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience | § 3.4(b) early termination charges are set in Attachment A with no cap and no "sole remedy" language; § 13.1 lets IBM change Attachment A on 90 days' notice. § 3.3 helpfully disapplies the charges where IBM is in breach. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 14.10 Assignment | Restriction is one-directional: IBM may assign freely, including to a competitor, with no notice or consent. Our M&A successor carve-out and a reasonableness standard exist; no affiliate carve-out for us and no restriction on IBM. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 14.16 Freedom of Action | No exclusivity, sole-source or all-requirements obligation; § 14.16 confirms each party may contract with others. Preferred position met. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 14.16 Freedom of Action | No non-compete, field-of-use or territory restriction on us; § 14.11 No Resale and the § 12.1/§ 14.17 licence-scope limits are ordinary boundaries, and § 14.19 limits only IBM's delivery obligations. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | § 3.2 Renewal | Auto-renews for a term equal to the previous term (multi-year renewals — walk-away) with a 90-day non-renewal notice, above the 60-day fallback ceiling; no renewal reminder and no uplift cap. |
| Medium | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience | One month's notice for us and no IBM convenience right are better than fallback and preserved; exit cost fails the fallback — uncapped early termination charges under § 3.4(b) and no refund of prepaid Charges in § 3.5. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 5.1 IBM Representations and Warranties | Reasonable care and skill plus compliance with laws, but no Deliverable/Materials conformance warranty, no warranty period and no remedy; § 5.4(c) delivers all Materials, including Type I, "AS IS." |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 3.5 Effect of Termination | § 3.5 addresses only payment; no exit assistance, data return, export or deletion obligation anywhere. § 14.18 covers contact information only; § 11.6 makes us responsible for Content with no return mechanic. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 14.3 Choice of Law | New York substantive law (preferred); no arbitration and no foreign or vendor-home venue. Absence of an express exclusive-venue designation is noted, not redlined. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | § 4.1 Charges | No pricing-parity, best-price or matching obligation on us; § 14.16 confirms freedom of action. Preferred position met. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume | Compliant | § 4.1 Charges | No minimum, take-or-pay or shortfall charge; § 11.5 leaves capacity changes to our determination and § 3.4 gives an unconditional monthly exit. Attachment A and Order Forms remain to be checked. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Needs review | § 11.3 Suspected Violations | No audit, inspection or verification right binds us — better than preferred. § 11.3 is a breach-investigation and remedy provision with no access to our premises, systems or records. Deterministic "audit frequency" check failed as an artifact of absence; no redline proposed. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Needs review | § 14.8 Personnel | No non-solicit, no-hire or inducement restriction on us — stronger than the mutual 12-month fallback. § 14.8 covers only each party's own personnel and subcontracting. Duration and carve-out checks are non-probative with no clause present; no redline proposed. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 14.12 Risk of Loss | No insurance clause anywhere; § 14.12 and § 5.3 address risk allocation and security features only. IBM operates the hosting environment and holds Customer Components, so the absence sits in walk-away territory. |

## Walk-away items

These are the findings the playbook classifies at or approaching walk-away. We would not sign without movement here.

1. **Customer indemnity for IBM's own Services — § 8.2(a)(3).** A one-way indemnity for any Services Recipient claim related directly or indirectly to the Services, with § 8.2(c) relief only where IBM's bad faith, wilful misconduct, gross negligence or breach caused the damages.
2. **Revocable licence — § 12.1.** The Base Components licence is expressly revocable with no standard, so IBM may withdraw it at discretion.
3. **Multi-year auto-renewal — § 3.2.** Renewal for a term equal in duration to the previous term, so a multi-year initial term auto-renews for multiple years, with a 90-day notice window.
4. **No vendor insurance.** No insurance obligation of any kind for a provider operating our hosting environment and holding Customer Components.
5. **Warranty package — § 5.1 with § 5.4(c).** No Deliverable conformance warranty, no warranty period and no remedy, with all Materials delivered "AS IS"; this approaches the walk-away position.

We also flag the two **critical** items as gating for signature even where not formally walk-away: the § 9 cap has no carve-out for confidentiality or data protection, and § 6 expressly makes §§ 9 and 10 prevail over the confidentiality agreement for information in the hosting environment.

## Next steps
